terms.definition: A type that protects its own data by letting only one task use it at a time.
terms.example: Use an actor to protect the shared counter.

terms.definition: The rule that only code inside an actor can touch its data directly, while others must use `await`.
terms.example: Actor isolation forces other code to use await.

terms.definition: A behavior where an actor can run other calls while one call waits at an `await`, so its state may change.
terms.example: Reentrancy means state can change at an await.

video.title: Actor, Actor Isolation & Reentrancy | Day 264
video.description:
Learn to explain how actors protect data and where they can surprise you: Actor, Actor Isolation & Reentrancy, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Actor - A type that protects its own data by letting only one task use it at a time.
Actor Isolation - The rule that only code inside an actor can touch its data directly, while others must use `await`.
Reentrancy - A behavior where an actor can run other calls while one call waits at an `await`, so its state may change.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Actor, Actor Isolation & Reentrancy in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Actor, Actor Isolation, Reentrancy 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Actor - A type that protects its own data by letting only one task use it at a time.
한국어: Actor: 한 번에 하나의 태스크만 사용하게 해서 자신의 데이터를 보호하는 타입

Actor Isolation - The rule that only code inside an actor can touch its data directly, while others must use `await`.
한국어: Actor Isolation: 액터 안의 코드만 데이터를 직접 만질 수 있고 나머지는 await를 써야 하는 규칙

Reentrancy - A behavior where an actor can run other calls while one call waits at an `await`, so its state may change.
한국어: Reentrancy: 한 호출이 await에서 기다리는 동안 액터가 다른 호출을 실행해 상태가 바뀔 수 있는 동작

landscape.hook: Can you explain Actor, Actor Isolation and Reentrancy in English?

dialogue.title: Coins in an actor
dialogue.setting: A counter that moved into an actor

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I moved my `coins` counter into an actor, and now the compiler wants await everywhere.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is actor isolation. Only code inside the actor can touch `coins` directly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An actor lets only one task use its data at a time, so the data stays safe.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I read `wallet.coins` without await? It is only a number.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Actor isolation does not allow it, even for a simple read. Use await.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. But is the actor always safe inside a long function?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Be careful with reentrancy. At each await, other calls can run on the actor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `coins` can change while my function waits?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. That is reentrancy. Check your values again after an await.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I forgot that. Last week I read `coins` before an await and used it after.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the classic reentrancy bug. Read it again after the await.
Use an actor to protect the shared counter.
